_comment: Tier-2 for skfem point_source#2, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: np.argmin on the vertex array snaps an off-node source to the nearest vertex with an error up to h/sqrt(2), it always returns an integer node id and never a barycentric position, and the fix is to find the containing triangle and split the load by barycentric coordinates. Ran: MeshTri().refined(4) (h = 0.0625, 289 DOFs), 200 random interior target points, then one concrete request at (0.3123, 0.7891) solved both by snapping and by barycentric distribution over the containing triangle found with m.element_finder(). Printed: argmin returns an int64; the maximum displacement over 200 targets is 0.042689 against the bound h/sqrt(2) = 0.044194, the mean is 0.022930 (a third of h) and NOT ONE target landed exactly on a vertex, so the rounding happens to essentially every off-node request. It is silent -- empty warning list, finite solution. The barycentric weights [0.0032, 0.3744, 0.6224] sum to 1 exactly and are all non-negative, the distributed load totals 1.000000000000, and the two placements differ by 1.56e-01 relative. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 builds the load for the requested point (0.3123, 0.7891) by barycentric distribution over the containing triangle instead of dropping the whole unit load on the argmin vertex ('f_round' at the pathology site) -- the documented fix. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 11 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 makes the snapped and the distributed right-hand sides identical, so the relative difference drops to 0 and 'the_two_placements_differ=True' disappears and the fixture goes red. The displacement statistics over the 200 random targets are properties of argmin itself and survive by design. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
